answer: Sybil resistance follows from binding each identity to a Wesolowski VDF whose output requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings. A verifier checks the compact proof, while an attacker creating many clones must complete a separate time-lock for each one. GPUs may run instances concurrently, but cannot shortcut the dependency chain, imposing a physical delay per identity. The anchor, delta, and shale parameters therefore do not remove the bottleneck.
